verify_binding reconstructs the 5-segment message with self.scope.as_ref() (authorization_grant.rs:685-690)

Companion suite tf3b_authorization_grant_binding_sig_one_signed_artifact.rs all 5 pre-existing tests PASS (A-1/A-2/A-3 + envelope round-trip + cross-surface byte-equality)

Intended at v1-beta freeze (no v1-signed grants on the wire outside test fixtures). No accidental cross-domain verification possible because v1 prefix and v2 prefix differ in the byte sequence.

findings.title: audience_pubkey is unsigned and exploitable at the ucan_blobs_protocol ARM 2 / ARM 5 split — SAME ATTACK CLASS as the L3-r1-1 scope hole the R6 R1 fix-pass just closed
findings.attack: An attacker Eve who obtains any valid AuthorizationGrant G issued for Alice (audience_pubkey=Alice_pk, audience_binding=hash(Alice_pk), scope, binding_sig over (domain||ucan||km||audience_binding||scope)) mutates only G.audience_pubkey = Eve_pk and presents G over Eve's iroh connection. ARM 2 (lines 437-460) reads request.grant.audience_pubkey and compares to connection EndpointId: Eve_pk == Eve_pk -> PASS. ARM 5 (lines 489-499) calls verify_binding(request.grant.audience_binding) — the binding-message reconstructs with audience=grant.audience_binding=hash(Alice) (unchanged), the signed payload also commits to hash(Alice), Ed25519 verify -> PASS. Eve gets Alice's data.
findings.why_l3_r1_1_fix_did_not_close_this: L3-r1-1 added scope to binding_message because scope was ARM-checked but unsigned. audience_pubkey is structurally identical: ARM 2 dispatches on it, but binding_message does NOT cover it. The R6 R1 fix-pass added scope but did not sweep the sibling unsigned-but-ARM-checked field in the same struct.
findings.v1_frozen_deferred_d15c_rationale_contra: docs/V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md Row D-15c (lines 529-533) states 'a cooperating attacker who forges audience_pubkey still cannot pass binding_sig verification' and treats this as defense-in-depth not a v1-beta security gap. This rationale is INVALID at the live ARM 2 / ARM 5 split — binding_sig DOES verify because it does not bind audience_pubkey, and ARM 2's pubkey-vs-EndpointId compare uses the unsigned field directly. The same logic Ben ratified to fold scope into binding_message applies verbatim here.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW — fold audience_pubkey into binding_message as a 6th segment (Option<[u8;32]> -> length-prefixed bytes, mirroring the scope_len_u32_le pattern). BUMP BINDING_SIG_DOMAIN v2 -> v3 to reflect the additional binding (mirrors the L3-r1-1 v1->v2 bump rationale). Add tf3b_audience_pubkey_substitution_post_sign_rejected.rs pin (both Some<->Some swap and None<->Some swap shapes). Retract D-15c's 'defense-in-depth only' framing and either close the row (binding now covers audience_pubkey, Option->non-Option promotion remains a separate ergonomics carry) or rewrite its rationale.
findings.non_defer_rationale: HARD RULE clause-(a) does not apply (in scope of this lens). Clause-(b) requires NAMED-NOW destination; D-15c exists but its rationale is contradicted by the live attack chain — promotion to FIX-NOW under the same precedent as L3-r1-1 is the correct disposition. Clause-(c) does not apply (this is the identical class as the just-closed L3-r1-1).

findings.title: L2-MIN-2 empty-DID defense-in-depth doc-claim does not match code — promised per-step audience check is missing
findings.site: crates/benten-caps/src/manifest_envelope_chain_validation.rs:289-294 vs the per-step loop at lines 306-354
findings.evidence: The doc-comment at lines 292-294 reads 'The check is also applied at every audience step (within the per-step loop below) for defense-in-depth.' Grep for as_str().is_empty() across the file returns only line 296 (the root_issuer pre-loop check). The per-step loop performs no empty-string audience_did check; if a chain step carries audience_did='' the validator only catches it indirectly via the chain-integrity audience_did != next.issuer_did check (and only if there IS a next step).
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW — either (a) add the promised per-step audience_did.as_str().is_empty() check inside the for loop at line 306+ (defense-in-depth as the comment claims), OR (b) delete the claim from the doc-comment (no false advertising) + document the chain-integrity coverage as the load-bearing path. Option (a) is the safer + 3-line fix and matches the L2-MIN-2 fix-pass intent.
findings.non_defer_rationale: MINOR — but the gap is a doc-vs-code drift introduced by the same L2-MIN-2 fix pass that landed at R6 R1; closes inline at R6 R2 fix-pass.

findings.title: ChainValidationOutcome::StepOutsideEnvelope is structurally overloaded for chain-integrity violations
findings.evidence: When chain-integrity check fails (step.audience_did != next.issuer_did, line 309), the validator returns step_outside_envelope(next) which builds a StepOutsideEnvelope variant. But the variant's docstring (line 172) states 'An intermediate plugin-DID's manifest shares policy does not permit the delegation step (Layer 2 ↔ Layer 3 mismatch).' A chain-integrity violation is structurally different from an envelope-policy mismatch: the failure has nothing to do with the issuer's manifest envelope. Mapping both into one variant loses attribution clarity for downstream error renderers and security audit logs.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW — add a ChainIntegrityViolation { broken_at_index: usize, observed_audience: Did, expected_issuer: Did } variant + map it to ErrorCode::PluginManifestInvalid (or a new ChainIntegrityViolated code if the catalog can absorb one). Update the helper or replace the step_outside_envelope call at line 313 with the new variant constructor. The 2-line fix preserves the existing ErrorCode mapping shape and gives operators a typed signal distinct from envelope-policy violations.
findings.non_defer_rationale: MINOR — clarity-of-attribution finding; trivial to fix inline at R6 R2 fix-pass; matches the pim-5 typed-error discipline.

findings.title: scope_len_u32_le prefix correctly disambiguates None vs Some(empty) — encoding contract holds
findings.evidence: binding_message encodes scope as len_u32_le || cbor_bytes. None => len=0, no bytes. Some(scope) => len=cbor.len(), then cbor bytes. The u32 cap is enforced via TryFrom and yields a typed Serialization error if cbor exceeds u32. The serde-derived RestrictedScope CBOR encoding is deterministic (no nondeterministic field ordering — all fields are explicit; BTreeMap is sorted) so the prefix length is stable across re-encodes. Symmetric Some<->None swap test (scope_removal_post_sign_rejected_by_binding_sig) PASS.
findings.disposition: OBS — positive confirmation; encoding contract is sound.

findings.title: RestrictedScope.contains 6-dimensional AND-composition is reflexive + transitive — walker contract holds
findings.evidence: contains() AND-composes per-dimension narrowing checks across all 6 dimensions. roots/edge_allowlist/label_allowlist share allowlist_subset_check (line 301-309) which encodes the unconstrained-None-contains-all + constrained-cannot-widen-to-unconstrained rule. label_denylist inverts (parent's denied set must be subset of child's). max_depth: None-self contains any; Some-self contains lower-or-equal Some-child. property_equalities: every parent constraint must be present and equal in child. Reflexive (s.contains(&s) true by construction across all 6 arms). Transitive by AND-composition of transitive per-dim relations.
findings.disposition: OBS — positive confirmation of the Spike H+1.1 composability claim.

Iterate-to-convergence per CLAUDE.md rule 9 Q5: full council re-review the edited artifact after the FP lands.
